title: Helm-to-Helm bilateral exchange envelope (BILAT-H2H-BUILD-SPEC.md §2.1)
description: Validates the H2H envelope PREDICATE shape (the object carried inside a dual-signed DSSE envelope's statement.predicate, predicateType #h2h_envelope_v1 — see hub/h2h-envelope.mjs, built on hub/envelope.mjs's existing Ed25519+ML-DSA-44 emitter/verifier). Layer 0 only (BILAT-H2H-BUILD-SPEC.md §2): a file/bundle exchange contract, no listener, no AINumbers-operated network component. `payload` carries an already OCG-conformant artifact produced independently of this exchange (evidence/matter bundle, counter-signed receipt, or cosigned checkpoint head) — this schema wraps it for transport, it does not restate the payload's own shape (cite, don't restate, per spec §2.1).

version.description: The WIRE-PROFILE version, distinct from the OCG SPEC.md version the payload conforms to (spec §5). A receiving Helm that does not recognize this value fails closed — see importH2HEnvelope in hub/h2h-envelope.mjs.

sender_org_id.description: The sending org's identity (did:key or LEI, per OCG identity conventions) — verification-side only, no registry of ours resolves it. The receiving Helm is expected to already hold this peer's public keys locally (out of band, per spec §2.2 — any transport the two orgs already trust).

payload_type.description: Which of the three cited artifact shapes `payload` carries (spec §2.1): matter_bundle = HELM-MATTER's evidence/matter bundle shape; counter_signed_receipt = BILAT-CSR's SPEC.md §27.12 humanAccountabilityRecord shape; cosigned_checkpoint_head = BILAT-COSIGN's SPEC.md §HEAD-1 checkpoint object carrying the ocg-head-bilateral-cosign@1 backing type. A receiving Helm that does not recognize this value fails closed.

payload.description: The cited artifact itself, verbatim — the same object the sending org already produced and holds in its own local state. Never a run input, never a request to execute anything (spec §4 run-input asymmetry). This schema does not constrain payload's internal shape; that is the cited artifact schema's job.
